subject: FinTechCo pricing follow-up: regional costs & token economics
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Quick recap + ask: token volumes, budget target, region preference

Alex — great talking earlier. Quick written recap and a few asks so we can size options and propose a concrete pilot.

Recap from call:
- Primary use case: customer support + transaction summarization (short prompts + long outputs)
- Current internal estimate: pilot ~10M tokens/month, expected growth to ~50M/mo in first 12 months, peak ~150M/mo
- Data residency: you mentioned EU-only requirement for EU customers; some US-origin data may be allowed to live in US.
- Key ask from your finance team: target unit economics (target $/1M tokens) and range for committed vs hosted pricing.

Please confirm (quick answers fine):
1) Pilot expected monthly tokens: confirm the ~10M/month figure
2) Target budget range for inference spend (examples: $500–$1,500 per 1M tokens) — what range would make a Dedicated pilot attractive?
3) Data residency: do all FinTechCo EU customer payloads *must* remain in EU, or is token-level redaction acceptable for some flows?

What we'll do next (from our side):
- I'll put together a short 1-page cost table for US vs EU hosted and Dedicated estimates (per 1M tokens), plus a sample mutual action plan for a 2–4 week EU Dedicated pilot.
- Attach SOC2 summary and a per-1M-token breakdown so your procurement team can start sizing.

If you can reply with the three quick items above, I'll turn this into a formal quote and pilot plan by Thursday.

Thanks — talk soon.

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(d) 415-555-0123 | dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Redwood Inference — inference that scales
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Feb 2027 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes, budget target, region preference

Thanks Dylan — good call. Answers inline.

1) Pilot tokens: confirmed ~10M/mo for a 30-day pilot (support + billing flows).
2) Forecast trajectory: month 3 we expect ~25M/mo, end of year ~50M/mo, multi-quarter peak planning at ~150M/mo.
3) Budget target: finance wants to see a unit cost near $1,000 per 1M tokens today for hosted; if Dedicated with a 12‑month commitment we could consider lower (target $600–$800/1M).
4) Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU for the EU product. For US customers, US residency is preferred but less strict. Token-level redaction is not sufficient for regulated EU flows.

I'll loop procurement once you share the pricing sheet. Procurement contact is procurement@fintechco.com.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alex.rivera@fintechco.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Feb 2027 08:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes, budget target, region preference

Alex — thanks for the clarity. Attached two files: price breakdown and our SOC2 summary for procurement. High-level estimates below (these are starting points; final numbers will be on the quote):

Assumptions: mixed prompt/response token ratio ~1:4 (short prompts, longer generated responses), standard open-model equivalent (Redwood-1-small); hosted = multi-tenant; Dedicated = reserved pool with predictable throughput and data isolation.

Hosted (pay-as-you-go):
- US region: ~$650 per 1M tokens
- EU region: ~$820 per 1M tokens (higher due to infra and cross-region costs)

Dedicated (committed monthly capacity, 12-mo term, includes guardrails/SLAs):
- 50M/mo commit (US): ~$450 per 1M tokens
- 50M/mo commit (EU): ~$580 per 1M tokens

Notes on differences:
- EU delta driven by higher cloud instance & egress pricing plus the operational overhead of EU-only control plane options and KMS integrations.
- Effective unit price will change if token mix is heavier on long responses (more output tokens) or if you choose larger model variants — we'll provide a model-level table in the formal quote.
- We can also offer a hybrid routing policy: EU customer traffic served in EU Dedicated pools; non-EU in US pools, with automatic fallback if EU capacity is constrained.

Example math for your pilot (10M tokens/mo, hosted EU):
- 10 * $820 = $8,200/mo
If you moved to a 50M/mo Dedicated commit in EU at ~$580/1M -> 50 * $580 = $29,000/mo (committed price; lower per-unit).

Next steps I propose:
1) You share a 7‑day token sample (anonymized) so we can validate the prompt/response mix and sequence lengths.
2) We'll produce a formal quote for: (a) 30-day EU Dedicated pilot at a small commit (e.g., 10–25M/mo) and (b) hosted fallback pricing.
3) Draft mutual action plan + PoC success criteria (latency SLO, error rates, cost cap).

Attaching: redwood-pricing-1m-token-breakdown.xlsx; redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Looping Marissa & Sean on finance/ops details — can you confirm the procurement contact and timeline for internal approvals?

Thanks,
Dylan

[Attachment: redwood-pricing-1m-token-breakdown.xlsx]
[Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf]
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 11:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask: token volumes, budget target, region preference

Thanks Dylan — that breakdown is exactly what procurement and finance needed.

Procurement will review the SOC2 doc and the pricing workbook this week. I'll aim to confirm:
- whether we can commit to a 50M/mo EU Dedicated pilot (likely needs exec OK)
- target timeline for pilot start: aiming for early March; I'll confirm by end of week.

Procurement loop: procurement@fintechco.com. Marissa — can you help with the finance model side if Dylan's team needs a forecast template?

I'll get back with a firm answer on commit level and timeline by Friday.

—Alex
